text.p: It was Montezuma's headdress that caught the eye of U.S. President Bill Clinton in a tour of Mexico's National Museum of Anthropology on Monday.

It was a large headdress, resplendent with turquoise-coloured peacock and quetzal feathers, and Clinton and Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo admired it on a two-hour tour of the museum soon after Clinton arrived on a three-day state visit.
Clinton told reporters he liked it but resisted suggestions that the headdress could be worked into his ceremonial routines in Washington.
"I think people would think I was putting on airs if I wore this," he said.

The presidents spent some time looking at an architect's model of the 14th-15th century city that is now Mexico City, known as Mexico Tenochtitlan. Clinton seemed impressed by the news that thousands of workers spent 100 to 150 years building the majestic city with pyramids.

"Imagine organising the work of thousands of people for hundreds of years," Clinton said. "And we are so impatient today -- all modern societies are so impatient. We say, 'how long will it take to organise this, 10 years?'"

In the room containing artifacts from the Olmecs civiliation, Clinton saw a statue of a heavily tattooed male with pierced sagging earlobes. He was reminded of a certain tattooed, bejeweled pro basketball player from the Chicago Bulls.
